source_text: Εἷς Θεὸς Πατὴρ Λόγου ζῶντος, σοφίας ὑφεστώσης καὶ δυνάμεως, καὶ χαρακτῆρος ἀϊδίου, τέλειος, τελείου γεννήτωρ· Πατὴρ Υἱοῦ μονογε νοῦς. Εἷς Κύριος, μόνος ἐκ μόνου, Θεὸς ἐκ Θεοῦ, χαρακτὴρ καὶ εἰκὼν τῆς θεότητος, Λόγος ἐνεργὸς, σοφία τῆς τῶν ὅλων συστάσεως περιεκτικὴ, καὶ δύναμις τῆς ὅλης κτίσεως ποιητικὴ, Υἱὸς ἀληθι νὸς ἀληθινοῦ Πατρὸς, ἀόρατος ἀοράτου, καὶ ἄφθαρτος ἀφθάρτου, καὶ ἀθάνατος ἀθανάτου, καὶ ἀΐδιος ἀϊδίου. Καὶ ἓν Πνεῦμα ἅγιον, ἐκ Θεοῦ τὴν ὕπαρξιν ἔχον· καὶ δι' Υἱοῦ πεφηνὸς, δηλαδὴ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, εἰκὼν τοῦ Υἱοῦ τελείου τελεία, ζωὴ ζώντων αἰτία, πηγὴ ἁγία, ἁγιότης ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγός· ἐν ᾧ φανεροῦται Θεὸς ὁ Πατὴρ, ὁ ἐπὶ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσι· καὶ Θεὸς ὁ Υἱὸς, ὁ διὰ πάν των· Τριὰς τελεία, δόξῃ καὶ ἀϊδιότητι καὶ βασι λείᾳ μὴ μεριζομένη, μηδὲ ἀπαλλοτριουμένη. Οὔτε οὖν κτιστόν τι, ἢ δοῦλον ἐν τῇ Τριάδι, οὔτε ἐπείσακτόν τι, ὡς πρότερον μὲν οὐχ ὑπάρχον, ὕστε ρον δὲ ἐπεισελθόν. Οὔτε οὖν ἐνέλιπέ ποτε Υἱὸς Πα τρὶ, οὔτε Υἱῷ Πνεῦμα· ἀλλ' ἄτρεπτος καὶ ἀναλλοίωτος ἡ αὐτὴ Τριὰς ἀεί.
thought_title: Confession of the one God, one Lord, one Spirit, and the perfect Trinity
orientation: Gregory Thaumaturgus opens his Declaration of Faith with a first-person confession of the Trinity, beginning with God the Father and moving through the Son to the Holy Spirit.
pass_a_gloss: One God, Father of the living Word, of subsisting wisdom and power, and of the eternal exact imprint, perfect, begetter of a perfect one; Father of the only-begotten Son. One Lord, alone from the alone one, God from God, exact imprint and image of the Godhead, active Word, wisdom that contains the constitution of all things, and power that makes the whole creation, true Son of a true Father, invisible of an invisible one, and incorruptible of an incorruptible one, and immortal of an immortal one, and eternal of an eternal one. And one Holy Spirit, having existence from God; and manifested through the Son, that is, to human beings, perfect image of the perfect Son, cause of life for the living, holy spring, holiness, giver of sanctification; in whom is manifested God the Father, the one over all things and in all things; and God the Son, the one through all things; perfect Trinity, in glory and eternity and kingdom not divided, nor alienated. Neither therefore is there any created thing, or servant in the Trinity, nor anything added later, as not existing before, but entering in later. Neither therefore did the Son ever fail the Father, nor the Spirit fail the Son; but unchanging and unalterable is the same Trinity always.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'Word' for Λόγος, identifying the Son as the living, active Word.
Glossary requires 'exact imprint' for χαρακτὴρ, the Son as the Father's perfect expression.
Glossary requires 'image' for εἰκὼν, used for the Son as image of the Godhead and the Spirit as image of the Son.
Glossary requires 'wisdom' for σοφία, identified with the Son as the wisdom that contains and orders all things.
Glossary requires 'power' for δύναμις, identified with the Son as the creative power of the whole creation.
Glossary requires 'Trinity' for Τριὰς, the perfect and undivided Trinity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Glossary requires 'only-begotten' for μονογενὴς, describing the unique sonship of the Son.
Glossary requires 'eternal' for ἀΐδιος, applied to the Father, the Son, and the Trinity.
Glossary requires 'unchanging and unalterable' for ἄτρεπτος καὶ ἀναλλοίωτος, describing the permanent identity of the Trinity.
Glossary requires 'created thing' for κτιστόν, denied of anything within the Trinity.
Glossary requires 'servant' for δοῦλον, denied of anything within the Trinity.
ἁγιότης is 'holiness' as a title of the Spirit, and χορηγός is 'giver', so the Spirit is the giver of sanctification, not 'that gives'.

pass_b_english: There is one God, the Father of the living Word, of subsisting wisdom and power, and of the eternal exact imprint: perfect, the perfect begetter, Father of the only-begotten Son. There is one Lord, alone from the Father alone, God from God, the exact imprint and image of the Godhead, the active Word, the wisdom that contains the constitution of all things, and the power that creates the whole creation: true Son of the true Father, invisible of the invisible, incorruptible of the incorruptible, immortal of the immortal, eternal of the eternal. And there is one Holy Spirit, who has existence from God and is manifested through the Son, that is, to human beings: the perfect image of the perfect Son, the cause of life for the living, the holy spring, holiness, the giver of holiness. In him God the Father is revealed, who is over all and in all, and God the Son, who is through all. The Trinity is perfect, undivided and unalienated in glory, eternity, and kingdom. Therefore nothing created, nothing servile, and nothing added later exists in the Trinity, as if it had not existed before and then entered in later. The Son was never lacking to the Father, nor the Spirit to the Son; but the same Trinity remains always unchanging and unalterable.

problems.why: ἁγιότης means 'holiness' as source/quality, not 'holiness' as separate item; should be 'holy one' or 'sanctity'

problems.quote: the begetter of the perfect one
problems.why: γεννήτωρ is 'begetter' but τελείου modifies it: 'begetter of the perfect one' inverts sense; should be 'perfect begetter'

edits.old: perfect, the begetter of the perfect one
the holy spring, holiness, the giver of sanctification
edits.new: the holy spring, the holy one, the giver of sanctification

fixed: τελείου γεννήτωρ: τελείου modifies γεννήτωρ, so 'perfect begetter' is correct.
ἁγιότης ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγός: ἁγιότης is a quality/source of holiness, so 'holy one' fits better than a separate 'holiness' item.

problems.why: English adds 'the holy one' not in source; source has 'holy spring, holiness giver of sanctification'.
problems.fix: the holy spring, the giver of sanctification

problems.why: Added phrase 'the holy one' has no equivalent in Greek text.
problems.fix: the holy spring, the giver of sanctification
problems.ruling: πηγὴ ἁγία = 'holy spring'; ἁγιότης = 'holiness'. 'The holy one' has no Greek equivalent.

edits.old: the holy spring, the holy one, the giver of sanctification
edits.new: the holy spring, the giver of sanctification

fixed: Removed 'the holy one' because the source has 'πηγὴ ἁγία, ἁγιότης ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγός' (holy spring, holiness, giver of sanctification), with no separate 'holy one' phrase.

problems.why: ἁγιότης means 'holiness', not 'sanctification'; the phrase is 'holiness, giver of holiness'.
problems.ruling: ἁγιότης means 'holiness'; English omits it, collapsing 'holiness, giver of holiness' into 'giver of sanctification'.

edits.old: the holy spring, the giver of sanctification
edits.new: the holy spring, holiness, the giver of holiness

fixed: The source phrase is ἁγιότης ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγός, which means 'holiness, giver of holiness'; the English omitted ἁγιότης and rendered ἁγιασμοῦ as 'sanctification' instead of 'holiness'. Fixed to 'holiness, the giver of holiness'.

dismissed.why: English adds comma making two items; source has one item: 'holiness-giver of holiness' or 'sanctification's holiness-giver'.
dismissed.note: Translators normally read 'ἁγιότης, ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγός' as two titles, holiness and the giver of sanctification, so the English is fair.

dismissed.quote: There is one God, the Father of the living Word, of subsisting wisdom and power, and of the eternal exact imprint: perfect, the perfect begetter
dismissed.why: Source says Father IS perfect and perfect begetter; English makes 'perfect' modify 'exact imprint' via colon, changing grammar.
dismissed.note: After the colon, 'perfect, the perfect begetter' plainly describes God the Father; the grammar is unchanged.
